# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a valve abnormality, which requires ongoing monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation issues, requiring occasional supplementation with nasogastric tube feeding.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypotonia, indicating weaker-than-normal muscle tone.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Hypotonia is a common feature in KBG syndrome, affecting muscle strength and coordination.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has palatal abnormalities, which may affect speech development and feeding.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Palatal abnormalities are a common feature in KBG syndrome, potentially leading to feeding difficulties and speech issues.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has palatal abnormalities, which may lead to feeding difficulties and speech issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Palatal abnormalities are a common feature in KBG syndrome, potentially leading to feeding difficulties and speech issues.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity, particularly with cold foods, indicating potential dental issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Tooth sensitivity is a common issue in KBG syndrome, especially with cold temperatures.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires additional help in school, with some going to a mainstream primary school but needing more support in secondary school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education needs vary widely among individuals with KBG syndrome, with some benefiting from mainstream schooling while others require specialized settings.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits behavioral differences, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and anxiety.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Behavioral differences are common in KBG syndrome, contributing to various challenges in social interaction and cognitive abilities.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has brachydactyly, a condition characterized by shortened fingers, and possibly clinodactyly, suggesting a slight curvature of the fifth finger.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Skeletal anomalies, such as brachydactyly and possible clinodactyly, are common in KBG syndrome, influencing hand and foot structures.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
- Regular dental check-ups to address tooth sensitivity and potential dental issues.
- Regular hearing reviews to monitor hearing status, especially during the first few years of life.
- Ophthalmological evaluation to address palatal abnormalities and potential feeding and speech issues.
- Cardiac review to monitor valve abnormalities and ensure proper heart function.
- Orthopedic assessment to evaluate the positioning of testes and assess for potential musculoskeletal issues.
- Palatal review to address feeding difficulties and potential speech issues.
- Monitoring growth velocity and considering endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has feeding difficulties, which can be challenging during meal times.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypotonia, which affects his muscle tone, and it is being managed.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Hypotonia is a common feature in KBG syndrome, affecting muscle tone.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient squints, indicating possible ocular motor dysfunction.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Squint is a potential feature of KBG syndrome, especially in infants.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty making himself understood when trying to communicate, suggesting possible auditory processing or speech-related issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Difficulty communicating is a common feature in KBG syndrome, potentially related to hearing or speech impediments.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has larger-than-normal front teeth, which is the main dental issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Larger-than-normal teeth are a common feature in KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires additional help in school, particularly with communication and possibly with academic challenges.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Communication difficulties are a common feature in KBG syndrome, requiring specialized educational support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has behavioral differences, specifically autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and anxiety.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Behavioral differences are a common feature in KBG syndrome, contributing to ASD, ADHD, and anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has brachydactylous fingers with a clinodactylic deformity of the fifth finger, indicating a shortened hand and a curved fifth finger.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Brachydactyly and clinodactyly are common features in KBG syndrome, leading to shorter fingers and a curved fifth finger.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Screen for hearing and vision issues early in life.
b) Refer for orthodontic evaluation and dental care.
c) Monitor growth and address any potential hormonal imbalances.
d) Consider a palate assessment if feeding difficulties or speech concerns are noted.

g) Evaluate for tethered cord syndrome, particularly if sacral dimples are present.
h) Address communication difficulties through speech therapy and behavioral interventions.
i) Manage hypotonia through physical and occupational therapies.
j) Provide educational support and accommodations based on the patient's needs.
